doc.title: Alan Broadbent interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 26, 2023

title: Confidence in arranging and treating the orchestra as an instrument
summary: He discusses the 'cringe moment' of first hearing a chart, and compares his struggle to move beyond the piano with Williams and Riddle for whom the orchestra was their instrument.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Did your confidence that your arrangements, your orchestrations, were going to work increase over the years? I’m thinking about those moments where you write a chart especially pre-computer, and you work for hours and days on it and the first time it gets played and you’ve got your fingers crossed.

Yeah. They call it the “cringe moment.” So you’d better be hearing what you’re hearing. That’s why somebody like John Williams, who sits there and just writes and then “Star Wars” comes out or something. You know it’s like that’s their instrument, you know what I mean? Nelson Riddle. That’s his instrument. For me I had to battle with the piano being my instrument, and finding a way to break away from it. You know now I come back to it, as I said before, and it is my slave. Because I’m not hearing that, I’m hearing an oboe and two clarinets, whatever.
Well your orchestral pieces are not necessarily realizations of your piano compositions. Is that a correct statement?

Yeah. I would say that perhaps the single note part of it would be the song part of it, yeah. But it has to have an atmosphere of orchestration. It’s got to be an orchestra you know? It’s got to have this feeling. Yeah, it’s not just a clarinet player and a harp and a you know. No, at all times, even if it’s a soloist, we have to have the feeling that it’s an orchestra you know, which is like a — how do I say — it should at all times to the audience feel like it is coming from an orchestra. Not just the strings over here and then the flutes over there and whatever. But there has to be this combination swimming around that makes it beautiful, beyond the mediocre.
